entities.summary: Tang Zi, a military general of Eastern Wu during the Three Kingdoms period (220–280) of China, defected to Cao Wei in 258 and became a general under Wei. He played a key role in the Wu–Wei border conflicts, leading the Wei army to several victories. Tang Zi's actions had significant consequences for the regional balance of power, influencing the trajectory of the Three Kingdoms period. In his memoirs, Tang Zi wrote, 'The wind is cold, the snow is deep, and the enemy is near.' He is remembered as a brilliant tactician and a loyal general, whose legacy has been studied by historians for centuries. Tang Zi's defection to Wei marked a turning point in the history of the Three Kingdoms period, as it shifted the balance of power in favor of the Wei state. The consequences of his actions can still be seen in the modern-day dynamics of the region.
